text:
anya: quick proposal — 'cascade + backfill' rollout for staged routing and prefix-cache backfill. small canaries in us-east -> eu-west -> ap-southeast with dependency flags for model-v2 and kv-backfill.

mike: sounds good. what's the ordering and why cascade instead of parallel?

anya: ordering: 1) enable feature-flag:model-v2-toggle for 1% us-east (canary), 2) start kv-backfill job scoped to that canary cohort, 3) watch telemetry, 4) increment to 10%, 5) open eu-west 5% with backfill job continuing, 6) full region roll. cascade reduces cross-region blast radius and lets backfill catch up before larger traffic.

jess: agree. we should ensure backfill is idempotent and rate-limited. DB writes from backfill should have a TTL and metrics. who owns the backfill job?

sam: eng-runtime will own the backfill runner, ops owns rate limits. implementation note: runner will read from prefix queue and write into KV with upsert. include a dry-run mode for first window.

raj: launch criteria proposal: p95 latency change <= +20ms, error-rate delta <= +0.5% absolute, model perplexity/quality check shows no regression on eval set, backfill throughput >= 5000 keys/min and no DB contention.

anya: +1 to those. add token-cost-per-request change <= +15% as a go/no-go for hosted customers.

alice-se: customer ask: two enterprise tenants want opt-in earlier; can we create per-tenant feature flag slices so they can be moved up?

mike: yes — support per-tenant override. we need guardrails: moves to opt-in must still obey region capacity and backfill queue priority. document how to pause opt-ins.

jess: fallback policy: if any of the three core signals breach for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> automatic rollback to previous variant and kill-switch alert to #oncall + paging if severity high. signals = p95 latency, 5xx rate, key-backfill-failure-rate.

anya: also include graceful degradation: if model-v2 is hotter than expected, route 20% of traffic to model-v1 variant (compatible) while backfill continues. this avoids full rollback.

sam: can we script that fallback in the routing policy? yes — policy snippet below:

```json
{
  "rule": "if p95_latency > threshold or error_rate > threshold -> route_fraction(0.2, model-v1); if persistent -> toggle flag off"
}
```

raj: metrics dashboard: need per-slice p50/p95, 5xxs, cost per token, backfill lag histogram, DB op latency. set alerts: p95 > +30ms OR 5xx rate > 1% -> SEV3; p95 > +80ms OR 5xx rate > 3% -> SEV2.

anya: testing plan: local stage -> internal dogfooding with 50 users -> small canary (1%) -> expanded canary (10%) -> region cascade. include automated double-run A/B for quality: 10% of canary kept as A/B compare vs control for NPS/QA checks.

alice-se: feature-flag config example for per-tenant override? please include in runbook.

mike: will add example and runbook steps: how to flip, how to pause backfill, how to invoke manual rollback. also include checklist for legal/security sign-off for private deployments.

jess: pre-launch gating: perf test with 2x expected QPS, backfill job stress test, chaos test (network partitions for kv), and storage quota check.

anya: timeline: dry-run next Wed, 1% canary Thurs, 10% Mon, eu-west Fri, ap-southeast following week. owner: anya (product), sam (runtime), mike (deploy/runbook), jess (observability).

rollout-bot: scheduled toggle model-v2-toggle at 2026-04-01T18:00Z for 1% us-east (dry-run).

mike: final note — communicate to affected customers with opt-in instructions + expected maintenance windows. keep #customer-success in the loop. :loudspeaker: 

anya: thanks — I'll draft the formal runbook and post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
